start.speaker: Sable
start.text: Spare a coin for a dying art, detective? No? Figures. Nobody down here has anything but time and bad lungs.

n1.speaker: Sable
n1.text: Trains stopped running honest years ago. But people still pass through. I see all of them. What do you want to know?

choices.text: People use this station for drops?
What do you see down here?

renner.speaker: Sable
renner.text: The kid with the recorder? Yeah. Rode the last train most nights, scared and stubborn. Last time I saw him he was white as the tiles. Said if anything happened to him, what he'd found was 'in the wall.' Then he tipped me a week's rent and never came back.

drops.speaker: Sable
drops.text: Down here? This whole station's a drop. No cameras that work, no cops that care. If a man wanted to hide something so it'd outlive him, the old luggage lockers behind me are where he'd put it.

drops2.speaker: Sable
drops2.text: 'In the wall' — the old luggage lockers, has to be. Go on. Whatever he died holding, it's still down here holding its breath.

see.speaker: Sable
see.text: I see the city's overflow. The ones it reclaimed and forgot to bury. Ask the harbor districts — half of them ride through here now, coughing, on their way to nowhere with the lights out. The city doesn't kill you loud, detective. It just stops running your train.

bye.speaker: Sable
bye.text: Suit yourself. Mind the gap. It's the only honest warning this city gives for free.
